fact: Digital Earth Africa and SASSCAL agreed to build the AgriWatch dashboard on DE Africa Earth-observation products for crop-cycle, rangeland and rainfall monitoring, with AgriWatch covering this country among the six SASSCAL states.

AICCRA reports that Zambia's National Crop Monitor, a GIS-based GEOGLAM tool using MODIS, VIIRS, CHIRPS, Landsat and Sentinel 2 data, was launched at a Lusaka workshop with provincial teams from Zambia's 10 provinces.

NASA Harvest reports an ESA WorldCereal workshop in Zambia in November 2025, hosted by CIMMYT, where 19 participants including national statistics offices and agricultural research institutes trained models and generated crop maps from 7,600 Zambian field samples collected in April 2025.

UNDP IRFF reports that Zambia's FISP crop index insurance, run through the Ministry of Agriculture's ZIAMIS platform, uses a weather index built on satellite-based data, with VIIRS and NDVI hybrid indices replacing degraded MODIS data.
UNDP IRFF says that by the 2023/24 season about 1.02 million FISP farmers were covered by crop index insurance, and a drought payout of over ZMW 800 million reached 500,000 farmers.
FEWS NET's October 2026 Southern Africa seasonal monitor reports below-average soil moisture in north-western Zambia from simulated remote-sensing data.
